claim: In chronic hepatitis C infection, CD16+ CD8 T cells displayed a late-stage effector phenotype with high levels of perforin with a restricted TCR profile.

claim: CD16 expression allows T cells to degranulate and exert cytotoxicity in an immune-complex-mediated, TCR-independent manner.
source: CD16 expression allows T cells to degranulate and exert cytotoxicity in an immune-complex-mediated, TCR-independent manner.

claim: CD16+ T cells from COVID-19 patients caused injury to microvascular endothelial cells and induced the release of neutrophil and monocyte chemoattractants.

claim: The proportions of activated CD16+ T cells and plasma levels of complement proteins upstream of C3a were found to be associated with fatal outcomes of COVID-19.

claim: CD16+ T cells may possess excessive cytotoxicity toward pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells, contributing to lung injury in PCP.
source: Given these findings and the observation of the highest proportion of CD16+ T cells in the fatal case of PCP, we hypothesize that these CD16+ T cells may possess excessive cytotoxicity toward pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells, contributing to lung injury in PCP, in addition to targeting P. jirovecii.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a hypothesis based on the data and literature.

claim: Anti-complement treatments may have the potential to treat severe PCP.
